$comment: Patterns that must not enter a public repo. Read by scripts/infra-leak.ts, which the
no-infra-leak CI job runs and scripts/infra-leak.unit.test.ts covers.
TWO CLASSES, and the distinction is the point.
patterns        Generic heuristics. They have legitimate exceptions — a security
control that refuses private ranges has to name them — so these
honour excludePaths.
EXTRA_INFRA_PATTERNS  Our actual coordinates: box address, real hostnames. Supplied
at runtime from a repository SECRET and deliberately absent from this
file, because writing the box IP into a public patterns file to stop
the box IP reaching a public repo is self-defeating. They ignore
excludePaths entirely: there is no file where a real coordinate is
legitimate. One pattern per line, # for comments.
excludePaths relaxes the HEURISTICS only. It never relaxes the secret patterns — which
is what makes it safe to exclude the SSRF guard, whose job is enumerating the very
ranges the heuristics look for.
Fork PRs receive no secrets, so the job warns rather than failing there. A scan that
quietly covers less than it claims is the vacuous pass this repo is arranged against,
so the reduced coverage is printed.
The ci.yml exclusion was removed once the scan logic moved to scripts/infra-leak.ts:
nothing in the workflow matches a pattern any more, and a stale exclusion is a hole
nobody remembers opening.
`farm[.]rip` was removed from this list. It is a real-looking hostname, and this file is
in the public repo — which is exactly the contradiction the two-class split above exists
to resolve. If it is a coordinate of ours it belongs in EXTRA_INFRA_PATTERNS, where it is
not published; if it is not, it does not belong here at all.
